title: Goodly Knight Frontline
summary: A small Goodly Folk starting layout centred on the Goodly Knight. It is a positioning sketch, not an official or ranked recommendation.
bestFor: Testing a simple front-and-back arrangement before committing to shop purchases.
strengths: Keeps the Goodly Knight forward so adjacent allies can benefit from its published base effect.
Leaves room to adapt to the live shop and unlocked cells.
Uses current public unit cards only.
weaknesses: No fixed loadout is assumed because shop rolls and board rules can change the right purchase.
It is not supported by published win-rate evidence.
A small company has less coverage when the formation breaks.
planningNote: Use the Builder to move the three cards after checking the live board; add equipment only after confirming the card's available slots.

title: Archer Cover Line
summary: A compact positioning idea that keeps the Archer behind two nearby Goodly Folk cards while you compare the live shop's gear options.
bestFor: Trying a clear backline role without treating a gear list as guaranteed.
strengths: The Archer's published base card has extended attack range.
The formation is easy to move, prune, and expand in the Builder.
No unsupported fixed item rolls are presented as fact.
weaknesses: The backline still needs protection from pathing and flank pressure.
It is a player-made starting point, not an official composition.
Unlocked cells and opponents can require a different shape.
planningNote: Start with the Archer protected, then revise the line after the active cells and available gear are known.

title: Wizard Space Plan
summary: An Ivo-led planning shell that gives the Wizard space instead of assuming a particular item roll or permanent best-in-slot loadout.
bestFor: Comparing a spell-oriented backline with a simple front screen.
strengths: Separates the Wizard from strength-dependent allies affected by its published base effect.
Leaves equipment choices open for the current shop and card capacity.
The compact board can be changed immediately in the Builder.
weaknesses: The plan does not prove a particular item will appear in a run.
Spacing is vulnerable when enemies reach the back row.
This is editorial theorycraft, not official balance advice.
planningNote: Keep room around the Wizard and treat the available gear list as a comparison tool rather than a preset shopping order.

title: Bone Host Flank Pair
summary: A small Bone Host workspace for comparing Skeleton Child and Skeleton Dog positions on the editable board.
bestFor: Exploring a two-card Bone Host starting shape without inventing a meta claim.
strengths: Uses two current public Bone Host cards.
The Skeleton Child's published base effect includes one battle respawn.
The layout is deliberately small and easy to revise.
weaknesses: It does not predict a live match outcome.
A two-unit test shape is not a complete company.
planningNote: Use it to compare positions, then expand it only with cards and equipment present in your own run.
